imc-1994-01.prompt:
a) Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ ($n\ge 2$) symmetric, invertible matrix with real positive elements. Show that $z_n\le n^2-2n$, where $z_n$ is the number of zero elements in $A^{-1}$.

b) How many zero elements are there in the inverse of the $n\times n$ matrix
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1&1&\cdots&1\\1&2&2&2&\cdots&2\\1&2&1&1&\cdots&1\\1&2&1&2&\cdots&2\\ \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\1&2&1&2&\cdots&\cdots\end{pmatrix}?$$
(The entry in row $i$, column $j$ is $1$ if $\min(i,j)$ is odd and $2$ if $\min(i,j)$ is even.)
imc-1994-01.answer: a) Every column of $A^{-1}$ has a positive and a negative entry, so at least $2n$ entries are non-zero. b) Exactly $n^2-2n$ zeros: $A^{-1}$ is tridiagonal with $b_{11}=2$, $b_{nn}=(-1)^n$, $b_{i,i+1}=b_{i+1,i}=(-1)^i$ and all other entries $0$.

imc-1994-02.prompt: Let $f\in C^1(a,b)$, $\lim\limits_{x\to a+}f(x)=+\infty$, $\lim\limits_{x\to b-}f(x)=-\infty$ and $f'(x)+f^2(x)\ge-1$ for $x\in(a,b)$. Prove that $b-a\ge\pi$ and give an example where $b-a=\pi$.
imc-1994-02.answer: $g(x)=\arctan f(x)+x$ is non-decreasing, so $\frac{\pi}{2}+a\le-\frac{\pi}{2}+b$. Equality: $f(x)=\cot x$ on $(0,\pi)$.

imc-1994-03.prompt: Let $S$ be a set of $2n-1$ different irrational numbers, $n\in\mathbb N$. Prove that there are $n$ different elements $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n\in S$ such that for all non-negative rational numbers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ with $a_1+a_2+\dots+a_n>0$ the number $a_1x_1+a_2x_2+\dots+a_nx_n$ is irrational.
imc-1994-03.answer: View $\mathbb R/\mathbb Q$ as a $\mathbb Q$-vector space and choose a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional $\varphi$ that is non-zero on all images of elements of $S$. By pigeonhole, $n$ of the $2n-1$ values $\varphi(x)$ have the same sign; those $n$ numbers work.

imc-1994-04.prompt:
Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and suppose that $F$ and $G$ are linear maps (operators) from $\mathbb R^n$ into $\mathbb R^n$ satisfying $F\circ G-G\circ F=\alpha F$.

a) Show that for all $k\in\mathbb N$ one has $F^k\circ G-G\circ F^k=\alpha kF^k$.

b) Show that there exists $k\ge1$ such that $F^k=0$.
imc-1994-04.answer: a) Induction: $F^{k+1}G-GF^{k+1}=F(F^kG-GF^k)+(FG-GF)F^k$. b) If $F^k\ne0$ for all $k$, the map $X\mapsto XG-GX$ on $n\times n$ matrices would have the infinitely many distinct eigenvalues $\alpha k$. (Alternatively, $\operatorname{tr}F^k=0$ for all $k$.)

imc-1994-05.prompt:
a) Let $f\in C[0,b]$, $g\in C(\mathbb R)$ and let $g$ be periodic with period $b$. Prove that $\displaystyle\int_0^b f(x)g(nx)\,dx$ has a limit as $n\to\infty$ and
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_0^b f(x)g(nx)\,dx=\frac1b\int_0^b f(x)\,dx\cdot\int_0^b g(x)\,dx .$$

b) Find
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_0^\pi\frac{\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 nx}\,dx .$$
imc-1994-05.answer: a) Split $[0,b]$ into $n$ intervals of length $b/n$; on each one $g(nx)$ runs over a full period, and $f$ is nearly constant (uniform continuity). b) With $f=\sin x$, $g=\frac{1}{1+3\cos^2x}$ and $b=\pi$: $\int_0^\pi\sin x\,dx=2$ and $\int_0^\pi g=\frac{\pi}{2}$, so the limit is $1$.

imc-1994-06.prompt:
Let $f\in C^2[0,N]$ and $|f'(x)|<1$, $f''(x)>0$ for every $x\in[0,N]$. Let $0\le m_0<m_1<\dots<m_k\le N$ be integers such that $n_i=f(m_i)$ are also integers for $i=0,1,\dots,k$. Denote $b_i=n_i-n_{i-1}$ and $a_i=m_i-m_{i-1}$ for $i=1,2,\dots,k$.

a) Prove that
$$-1<\frac{b_1}{a_1}<\frac{b_2}{a_2}<\dots<\frac{b_k}{a_k}<1 .$$

b) Prove that for every choice of $A>1$ there are no more than $N/A$ indices $j$ such that $a_j>A$.

c) Prove that $k\le3N^{2/3}$ (i.e. there are no more than $3N^{2/3}$ integer points on the curve $y=f(x)$, $x\in[0,N]$).
imc-1994-06.answer: a) By the mean value theorem $b_i/a_i=f'(x_i)$ with $m_{i-1}<x_i<m_i$, and $f'$ is strictly increasing with $|f'|<1$. b) $A\cdot\#\{j:a_j>A\}<\sum a_j\le N$. c) The distinct fractions $b_i/a_i\in(-1,1)$ with $a_i\le A$ number at most $A^2$, so $k<N/A+A^2$; take $A=N^{1/3}$.

imc-1994-07.prompt:
Let $f\in C^1[a,b]$, $f(a)=0$ and suppose that $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\lambda>0$, is such that
$$|f'(x)|\le\lambda|f(x)|$$
for all $x\in[a,b]$. Is it true that $f(x)=0$ for all $x\in[a,b]$?

imc-1994-08.prompt:
Let $f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be given by $f(x,y)=(x^2-y^2)e^{-x^2-y^2}$.

a) Prove that $f$ attains its minimum and its maximum.

b) Determine all points $(x,y)$ such that $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x,y)=\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}(x,y)=0$ and determine for which of them $f$ has a global or local minimum or maximum.
imc-1994-08.answer: $\max f=e^{-1}$ at $(\pm1,0)$, $\min f=-e^{-1}$ at $(0,\pm1)$. The critical points are $(0,0),(\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)$, and $(0,0)$ is a saddle point (no extremum).

imc-1994-09.prompt:
Let $f$ be a real-valued function with $n+1$ derivatives at each point of $\mathbb R$. Show that for each pair of real numbers $a,b$, $a<b$, such that
$$\ln\left(\frac{f(b)+f'(b)+\dots+f^{(n)}(b)}{f(a)+f'(a)+\dots+f^{(n)}(a)}\right)=b-a$$
there is a number $c$ in the open interval $(a,b)$ for which $f^{(n+1)}(c)=f(c)$. (Here $\ln$ denotes the natural logarithm.)
imc-1994-09.answer: Apply Rolle's theorem to $g(x)=e^{-x}\big(f(x)+f'(x)+\dots+f^{(n)}(x)\big)$, which satisfies $g(a)=g(b)$ and $g'(x)=e^{-x}\big(f^{(n+1)}(x)-f(x)\big)$.

imc-1994-10.prompt:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ diagonal matrix with characteristic polynomial
$$(x-c_1)^{d_1}(x-c_2)^{d_2}\cdots(x-c_k)^{d_k},$$
where $c_1,c_2,\dots,c_k$ are distinct (which means that $c_1$ appears $d_1$ times on the diagonal, $c_2$ appears $d_2$ times on the diagonal, etc., and $d_1+d_2+\dots+d_k=n$). Let $V$ be the space of all $n\times n$ matrices $B$ such that $AB=BA$. Prove that the dimension of $V$ is
$$d_1^2+d_2^2+\dots+d_k^2 .$$
imc-1994-10.answer: $(AB-BA)_{ij}=(a_{ii}-a_{jj})b_{ij}$, so $B$ commutes with $A$ if and only if $b_{ij}=0$ whenever $a_{ii}\ne a_{jj}$. The free entries are the pairs $(i,j)$ with $a_{ii}=a_{jj}$, and there are $\sum d_m^2$ of them.

imc-1994-11.answer: Build $\pi$ greedily: if $y$ is the current partial sum, the remaining vectors add up to $-y$, so one of them, $x_r$, has $(y,x_r)\le0$. Taking it next keeps $\|\text{partial sum}\|^2\le\sum(\text{squared norms used})$.

imc-1994-12.prompt:
Find
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\ln^2N}{N}\sum_{k=2}^{N-2}\frac{1}{\ln k\cdot\ln(N-k)} .$$
(Here $\ln$ denotes the natural logarithm.)
